newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX firms slightly on Slovakofarma gains.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX firms slightly on Slovakofarma gains.

text.p: Slovak blue chips were mostly quiet in thin trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, but the official SAX index firmed 1.59 points to 196.37 on gains by drug producer Slovakofarma.
Slovakofarma rose 390 to 4,390 crowns, pushed by investor demand amid the news of a planned capital increase, including a rights issue later this year.
"We expected Slovakofarma to increase as some investors seemed to be accumulating their holdings to obtain a larger portion of the planned new issue," said Bohus Betko of ING Barings.

Slovakofarma on Monday confirmed market rumours that it was preparing an equity increase through the issue of 230,765 bearer shares at a nominal value of 1,000 crowns with prepurchase rights for current shareholders. An unspecified tranche of the planned issue should be convertible to GDRs.
The most heavily-weighted issue, oil refiner Slovnaft, led trading on the BSE floor, matching 3,393 shares and closing up 15 crowns at 1,000.
Betko said Slovnaft's price rose on expectations of the approval of its dividend policy at an annual shareholders' meeting next Thursday.
Stockbrokers expect Slovnaft to pay a dividend of around 20 crowns per share.
Steel maker VSZ closed unchanged at 730 crowns, with dealers saying there was very little demand for it at the moment and that they did not expect more lively trading until the AGM later this year.
Overall volume fell to 197,951 shares, from 220,928 traded on Friday, while turnover decreased to 97.82 million crowns from 125.16 million.
